source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Electrical - Body and Chassis, p.12-56

procedures.title: Wiper cover panel vacuum relay: replace
steps: Move the 4 hoses from the old relay to the new one, matching each hose stripe color to the letter on the relay pipe: G green, Y yellow, R red.

procedures.title: Wiper cover panel manual override vacuum switch: replace
steps: Remove the switch screw and push the switch rearward to free it from the bracket.
Move the vacuum hoses to the new switch.
Set the new switch in place and fasten it with the screw.
notes: The switch opens the wiper cover panel; it is under the left side of the instrument console, at the far right of the controls.

procedures.title: Horn relay-buzzer: buzzer check
steps: Make sure the key is fully in the ignition switch.
Open the driver's door and watch the dome lamp.
If neither dome lamp nor buzzer works, check the door switch.
If the dome lamp lights but no buzz, remove the horn relay-buzzer and find terminals No. 1 and No. 4.
Jumper terminal No. 4 to ground; with slip-on terminals, slide a prod into the harness connector to make contact.
notes: The horn relay and key reminder buzzer are one unit; terminal numbering is the same on all models though type and location vary (see figures 87 and 88 in the manual).

Buzzer: with the key in and the driver's door open, terminal No. 4 is grounded through the door switch; current through the coil opens the buzzer contacts, which re-close, many times a second. Closing the door or pulling the key stops it.
Horn: closing the horn switch grounds the coil, the armature closes the horn relay contacts and the horns get battery feed; the buzzer contacts stay open meanwhile.
